items.name: agent/session.create
items.summary: Open a stateful, tool-using agent session bound to the calling user. Validates `agent_submode` ∈ {auto, fixed}; `fixed_client_id` is required when `agent_submode='fixed'`. For one-shot completion use `agent/complete` instead. Identity (`user_id`, `executa_id`) is derived from the sampling_token claims — the plugin cannot override it.
items.signature: session_create(*, agent_submode: Literal['auto','fixed'] = 'auto', fixed_client_id: str | None = None, label: str | None = None, quota_caps: dict | None = None, ttl_seconds: int = 600) -> dict

params.name: agent_submode
params.summary: Multi-turn agent mode. `auto` rotates `client_id` per turn; `fixed` pins one.
notes: `auto` is the recommended default for most plugins.
`fixed` additionally requires `fixed_client_id` AND a matching entry in `llm_grant.agent.allowed_fixed_client_ids`, otherwise Anna server returns `AGENT_ERR_NOT_GRANTED` (-32041).

params.name: fixed_client_id
params.summary: Pin one `client_id` for the whole session.
notes: Only meaningful when `agent_submode='fixed'`.
Under `submode='auto'` it is silently stored on the session row but has no runtime effect.
Must appear in `llm_grant.agent.allowed_fixed_client_ids` or the call is rejected.

params.name: label
params.summary: Human-readable label shown in the user's session console.
notes: Max 120 chars; longer values are rejected at the Anna server pydantic boundary (HTTP 422).
When omitted, Anna agent substitutes the plugin display name from `ctx.plugin_name`.

params.name: quota_caps
params.summary: Per-session quota / tool-scope override.
notes: **Default when omitted**: Anna server injects `inherit_host_tools=True`, so the agent session inherits the host Copilot's full tool kit (`granted_tools` returns `['*']`).
To restrict tools, pass an explicit dict, e.g. `{"inherit_host_tools": False, "allowed_tools": ["tool_a", "tool_b"]}`.
Anna server intersects the result with the user's grant and may clamp further; the effective value is reflected back in `granted_tools` on the response.

params.name: ttl_seconds
params.summary: Session-token lifetime in seconds; Anna agent caches the bearer for this duration.
notes: Bounded by `0 < ttl_seconds ≤ MAX_APP_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS` (7200).

Anna server pydantic rejects out-of-range with HTTP 422; bridge has no local validation, so the failure surfaces as `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR` (-32046) (the generic `Exception` arm in `_session_create`), **not** `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`.

returns.desc: `{app_session_uuid, expires_in, thread_id, agent_submode, fixed_client_id, granted_tools, executa_id}` — the bearer `token` is stripped by Anna agent before returning; the handler keeps it in-memory and reuses it for subsequent `session.run` / `session.cancel` / `session.history` calls on the same `app_session_uuid`.

errors.name: AGENT_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: `sampling_token` missing from handler `ctx` — host did not authorize agent reverse-RPC for this plugin. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_NOT_GRANTED`. Wire `error.data.errorCode` keeps the `AGENT_` prefix (unique to -32041 in this namespace).

errors.name: INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: `_validate_create` rejected the params (e.g. `agent_submode='fixed'` without `fixed_client_id`, non-string `label`, etc.). SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`.

errors.name: SUBMODE_MISMATCH
errors.desc: Propagated verbatim from Anna server `/copilot/app/sessions` when `agent_submode` or `fixed_client_id` diverges from the user grant (e.g. `fixed` requested but the grant only allows `auto`, or `fixed_client_id` not in `llm_grant.agent.allowed_fixed_client_ids`). Bridge does not re-shape; SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_SUBMODE_MISMATCH`.

errors.name: QUOTA_EXCEEDED
errors.desc: User plan-level LLM/agent quota exhausted at session mint time. Propagated verbatim from upstream `_ServerRpcError`. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`.

errors.name: PROVIDER_ERROR
errors.desc: Catch-all for upstream session-mint failures: HTTP 422 (out-of-range `ttl_seconds`, malformed `label > 120`), HTTP 5xx, transport failures, or malformed response missing `app_session_uuid`/`token`. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR`. **Does NOT preserve the upstream `errorCode`** — it is flattened into a string message (`upstream error: …`).

limitations: ⚠ **Wire `error_name` ≠ Python SDK constant.** Plugin code that reads `error.data.errorCode` from the raw JSON-RPC frame sees the short form (`INVALID_REQUEST`, `SUBMODE_MISMATCH`, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `PROVIDER_ERROR`) per `AGENT_ERROR_NAMES` in the Anna Agent runtime. Only `AGENT_NOT_GRANTED` (-32041) keeps the `AGENT_` prefix — the rest do not. **Match on the numeric code OR on the short name** — do not compare against the SDK constant string.

⚠ **`-32031 SAMPLING_ERR_NOT_GRANTED` can leak out of this method.** When the `sampling_token` JWT claims have no `user_id` (or it's not a string), `_owner_from_ctx` raises code `-32031` — a *sampling* namespace error — but `_err()` cannot find `-32031` in `AGENT_ERROR_NAMES`, so wire `error_name` degrades to the generic fallback `"AGENT_ERROR"`. Plugins switching on numeric code only will see an orphan `-32031` from `session.create`.
`ttl_seconds`, `label` length and other Anna-server-side bounds are **not** validated by the bridge — out-of-range values fail late with `PROVIDER_ERROR (-32046)`, not `INVALID_REQUEST (-32043)`.

Identity (`user_id`, `executa_id`) is derived from `sampling_token` claims by `_owner_from_ctx`; the plugin cannot override it. The bearer `token` returned by Anna server is **stripped before being handed back** to the plugin (`out.pop("token", None)`) and kept only in the handler's in-memory `TokenCache`, keyed by `(uuid, owner)` with TTL = `expires_in` (default 600s) and a 30s safety margin. Cache is bounded at `_TOKEN_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 4096` with GC at 8192.

items.name: agent/session.run
items.summary: Submit one turn on an existing agent session. The Anna agent consumes the upstream SSE stream from Anna server `/copilot/app/agent`, tags every frame with `seq` + `stream_id`, and returns the full ordered `frames` array in a single JSON-RPC response — i.e. **buffered streaming**, not true streaming. Hard-capped at `_MAX_FRAMES_PER_RUN = 4096` frames per run; exceeding the cap aborts with `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR` (-32046).
items.signature: session_run(*, app_session_uuid: str, content: str, attachments: list[dict] | None = None, recursion_limit: int = 8, run_id: str | None = None, allowed_tools: list[str] | None = None, modelPreferences: dict | None = None, system: str | None = None) -> dict

params.name: app_session_uuid
params.summary: The session handle returned by `agent/session.create`.
notes: Must start with `aps_`.
The Anna agent looks up the cached `app_session_token` by `(uuid, owner)`; if missing or expired → `AGENT_ERR_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` (-32042).

params.name: content
params.summary: Turn content (user / plugin input).
notes: Validated as a non-empty string; whitespace-only is rejected with `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST` (-32043).

params.name: attachments
params.summary: Optional attachments forwarded verbatim to Anna server.
notes: The Anna agent does not parse or validate the payload — shape is whatever Anna server `/copilot/app/agent` currently accepts.

params.name: recursion_limit
params.summary: Max agent tool-call depth for this turn.
notes: The Anna agent does not range-check the value; it is forwarded as-is.
Anna server pydantic enforces `1 ≤ recursion_limit ≤ 32` (`Field(ge=1, le=32)`). Out-of-range values → HTTP 422, surfaced as `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR` (-32046), **not** `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`.

params.name: run_id
params.summary: Idempotency / correlation id for `session.cancel`.
notes: Auto-generated as `run_{16hex}` when omitted.
Echoed back in the response and required by `agent/session.cancel`.

params.name: allowed_tools
params.summary: Per-turn tool whitelist; overrides the session-level `quota_caps.allowed_tools` for this run only.
notes: Forwarded verbatim to Anna server as the `allowed_tools` field.
Anna server intersects this with the user's grant; tools outside the grant are silently dropped.
Pass `[]` to disable all tools for this turn (pure LLM reply).

params.name: modelPreferences
params.summary: MCP-style model hint, e.g. `{"hints": [{"name": "gpt-4o"}], "costPriority": 0.2}`.
notes: Camel-case to match the MCP wire spec and Anna server's `_AgentRunBody.modelPreferences` field.
Snake-case alias `model_preferences` is also accepted by the bridge and rewritten on the way out.
Anna server may ignore hints that fall outside the user's enabled model set.

params.name: system
params.summary: Per-turn system prompt override; prepended to the turn on Anna server.
notes: Forwarded verbatim as the `system` field on the REST body.
Does not mutate session state — next turn falls back to the session default unless re-supplied.

returns.desc:
Response shape: `{run_id, stream_id, frames, final, frame_count}`.

**Frame envelope** — every entry in `frames` is `{event, seq, stream_id, ...}`. `seq` and `stream_id` are injected by the Anna agent so plugin SDKs can later upgrade to true streaming without protocol churn.

**Event types** carried from upstream: `delta` (incremental text), `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `model_token`, `usage`, and `final`.

**Synthesized final** — Anna server's OpenAI-style SSE does not emit a `final` event; when no upstream `final` arrived, the Anna agent appends a synthesized one: `{event: 'final', text: <joined deltas>, stream_id, seq, synthesized: True}`. This guarantees the plugin always has a single authoritative terminal frame.

There is **no top-level `text` field** — aggregated assistant text lives in `final.text`.

errors.name: AGENT_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: `sampling_token` missing from handler `ctx`. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_NOT_GRANTED`.

errors.name: SESSION_NOT_FOUND
errors.desc: `app_session_uuid` not in handler `TokenCache` for this owner — token expired (default TTL 600s, 30s safety margin), the session was deleted, or the uuid belongs to a different `(user_id, executa_id)`. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`.

errors.name: INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: `_validate_run` rejected the params (e.g. empty/whitespace-only `content`, non-string `app_session_uuid`, missing `aps_` prefix). SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`.

errors.name: QUOTA_EXCEEDED
errors.desc: User plan-level quota exhausted mid-run, propagated verbatim from upstream `_ServerRpcError`. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`.

errors.name: PROVIDER_ERROR
errors.desc: Catch-all: upstream SSE failure, transport error, HTTP 422 (out-of-range `recursion_limit`), **OR the synthetic frame-cap abort** when the buffered stream exceeds `_MAX_FRAMES_PER_RUN = 4096`. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR`. Original upstream `errorCode` is **flattened to a string message** and not preserved.

errors.name: RATE_LIMITED
errors.desc: User or session rate-limited at the LLM provider. Propagated verbatim from upstream. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_RATE_LIMITED`.

errors.name: TOOL_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: `allowed_tools` (per-turn) or session-level tool list includes a tool that is not in the user's grant. Propagated verbatim from upstream. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_TOOL_NOT_GRANTED`. Note: upstream may also silently drop ungranted tools instead of raising — depends on call site.

limitations: ⚠ **Wire `error_name` ≠ SDK constant** — see `session.create` Known limitations for the full mapping. `session.run` is the most exposed surface: 7 distinct codes, 4 of them propagated verbatim from Anna server.

⚠ **Original upstream `errorCode` is lost** when the bridge wraps an upstream failure in `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR` via the `except Exception` arm (e.g. HTTP 422 from Anna server pydantic for `recursion_limit > 32`). Plugins cannot distinguish 'quota' / 'rate limit' / 'recursion-limit' failures from each other by code alone — only the message string `upstream error: …` differs. To preserve upstream codes, Anna server must emit a proper `_ServerRpcError` (`-32044`/`-32045`/`-32047`/`-32048`), which the `except _ServerRpcError: raise` arm propagates verbatim.

**Buffered streaming, not true streaming.** Every upstream SSE frame is buffered in-memory and the full ordered array is returned in a single JSON-RPC response. Hard-capped at `_MAX_FRAMES_PER_RUN = 4096` per run (host keepalive frames are filtered out and do NOT count); exceeding the cap raises `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR`, drops everything buffered so far, and best-effort cancels the run upstream.

**Client-side abort cleans up upstream.** If the buffered consume fails (600 s reverse-RPC budget exhausted, frame cap, transport error), the bridge sends `agent/session.cancel` upstream before raising — the run no longer keeps executing server-side for up to 30 min after the plugin has given up. `error.data.cancelled_upstream: true` marks this path.

**Per-user concurrency.** The owning user is limited to 10 concurrent agent runs platform-wide (`APP_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT`, jsonrpc `-32020`, retryable) — counted together with iframe Host-API runs of the same user.

**Synthesized `final` frame** — Anna server's OpenAI-style SSE never emits a true `final` event, so when text was accumulated but no upstream `final` arrived, the bridge appends `{event: 'final', text: <joined deltas>, stream_id, seq, synthesized: True}`. Plugin SDKs should treat the last frame as authoritative regardless of `synthesized`.

items.name: agent/session.cancel
items.summary: Cancel an in-flight `session.run`. Best-effort; the upstream may still emit a final frame.
items.signature: session_cancel(*, app_session_uuid: str, run_id: str) -> dict

params.name: run_id
params.summary: The `run_id` returned by (or passed into) `session.run`.

returns.desc:
Response shape: `{cancelled: bool, run_id: str}` — the `run_id` is echoed back verbatim so plugins can correlate the ack with the originating `session.run` call.

`cancelled: true` means the cancel signal was durably recorded server-side: a still-queued run is dropped before it starts, and a running run stops at the next poll checkpoint (an in-flight provider call still completes first). It is an acknowledgement, NOT a confirmation the run already stopped. `cancelled: false` means the signal could not be recorded (e.g. signalling backend unavailable) — safe to retry.

errors.name: AGENT_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: `sampling_token` missing from handler `ctx`. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_NOT_GRANTED`.

errors.name: SESSION_NOT_FOUND
errors.desc: `app_session_uuid` not in handler `TokenCache` for this owner. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`. Cancel is NOT idempotent — unlike `session.delete`, cancelling an unknown uuid hard-fails.

errors.name: INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: `app_session_uuid` (must start with `aps_`) or `run_id` is missing/non-string. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`.

errors.name: PROVIDER_ERROR
errors.desc: Upstream cancel call failed (transport error or 5xx). SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR`. Note: `cancelled: False` in the success response is **not** an error — it means the signal could not be recorded; retry.

limitations: ⚠ **Wire `error_name` ≠ SDK constant** — see `session.create` Known limitations.

**Best-effort, not transactional.** A successful `session.cancel` does not guarantee the in-flight `session.run` will return early; the upstream may have already buffered enough frames to emit a complete `final`. Plugins should always handle a normal-looking `run` response arriving after a cancel ack.
If the run already finished, the signal is recorded but has no effect — still `cancelled: true`.

items.name: agent/session.history
items.summary: Read the persisted transcript of an agent session as MCP-shaped messages. Backed by the LangGraph checkpoint that `session.run` writes into; safe to poll, idempotent, and never mutates state. Use this to rehydrate UI after a plugin restart, sync across devices, or audit a completed conversation.
items.signature: session_history(*, app_session_uuid: str, limit: int = 50, cursor: str | None = None) -> dict

params.name: app_session_uuid
params.summary: The session uuid to read; must match the cached token entry.

params.name: limit
params.summary: Page size; out-of-range values are rejected.
notes: Bridge-side range check (`agent.py:_session_history`): values outside `[1, 200]` raise `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST` (-32043) — the bridge does **not** clamp silently. Anna server applies the same `[1, 200]` clamp on its side as defense in depth.
Counts raw checkpoint messages, not turn pairs — a single user turn that triggered N tool calls contributes `1 + 2N` entries.

params.name: cursor
params.summary: Opaque pagination token returned by the previous page's `next_cursor`.
notes: First call: pass `None` (or omit).
Round-trip the value verbatim; do not parse or mutate it — the format is intentionally opaque and may switch from offset-based to time-based without protocol churn.
Passing a malformed cursor raises `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`.

returns.desc:
Response shape: `{messages, next_cursor, _meta}`.

**`messages`** is an array of MCP-shaped dicts:

- `{role: 'user', content}` — human turn.
- `{role: 'assistant', content, tool_calls?}` — model turn; `tool_calls` is `[{id, name, args}]` when the assistant invoked tools.
- `{role: 'tool', content, tool_call_id, tool_name, is_error}` — tool execution result; `content` longer than 10 000 chars is truncated server-side and suffixed with `\n...[truncated]`.
- `{role: 'system', content}` — system prompt, when present in state.

**`next_cursor`** is `None` when the page reached the tail; otherwise pass it back as `cursor` on the next call to continue.

**`_meta`** carries debug + pagination context: `{thread_id, total, has_more, kind}`. Sessions of `kind == 'complete'` have no thread and always return `messages: []`, `_meta.thread_id: null`, `_meta.kind: 'complete'`. A freshly minted agent session before any `session.run` returns `messages: []` with `_meta.total: 0`.

errors.name: AGENT_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: `sampling_token` missing from handler `ctx`. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_NOT_GRANTED`.

errors.name: SESSION_NOT_FOUND
errors.desc: `app_session_uuid` not in handler `TokenCache` for this owner. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`.

errors.name: INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: `app_session_uuid` malformed (must start with `aps_`), `limit` not an integer, `limit` outside `[1, 200]`, or `cursor` not a string/null. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`. Note: `limit` is **rejected, not clamped** — see param notes.

errors.name: PROVIDER_ERROR
errors.desc: Upstream history fetch failed (transport error or 5xx). SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR`.

limitations: ⚠ **Wire `error_name` ≠ SDK constant** — see `session.create` Known limitations.
**Idempotent and safe to poll** — never mutates session state.

Sessions of `kind == 'complete'` always return `messages: []` with `_meta.kind: 'complete'` and `_meta.thread_id: null` — they have no LangGraph checkpoint to read. This is the expected shape, not an error.
`cursor` format is intentionally opaque; round-trip verbatim. The server may switch from offset-based to time-based without protocol churn, so plugins MUST NOT parse or mutate it.

items.name: agent/session.delete
items.summary: Drop the session and its history. **Idempotent** — calling on an unknown or already-deleted uuid still resolves successfully. The bridge always evicts the cached token before returning, so a follow-up `session.run` against the same uuid will fail with `AGENT_ERR_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`.

params.name: app_session_uuid
params.summary: The session uuid to drop; must start with `aps_`.

returns.desc:
Response shape: `{deleted: True, app_session_uuid, already_gone?}`.

`deleted` is always `True` on success — the call is idempotent and never reports a 'nothing to do' failure.

`app_session_uuid` echoes the input so plugins can correlate batched deletes without re-threading the request id.

`already_gone: True` is set **only** when the bridge had no cached token for the uuid (e.g. another worker deleted it, the cache TTL expired, or the uuid was never created in this process). When the upstream `/copilot/app/sessions/{uuid}` DELETE succeeds normally, this field is **absent** and only `{deleted: True}` is returned verbatim from Anna server.

errors.name: AGENT_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: `sampling_token` missing from handler `ctx`. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_NOT_GRANTED`.

errors.name: INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: `app_session_uuid` malformed (must start with `aps_`). SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`.

errors.name: PROVIDER_ERROR
errors.desc: Upstream DELETE call failed (transport error or 5xx). SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR`. The cached token is **always** evicted in the `finally` block before this error surfaces.

limitations: ⚠ **Wire `error_name` ≠ SDK constant** — see `session.create` Known limitations.

**Idempotent — does NOT raise `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`.** Calling on an unknown or already-deleted uuid returns `{deleted: True, app_session_uuid, already_gone: True}` and never hits the upstream. Distinct from `session.cancel` / `session.run` / `session.history`, which all hard-fail on cache miss.

**Cache eviction is unconditional.** Even when the upstream DELETE raises `PROVIDER_ERROR`, the bridge has already evicted the cached token in the `finally` clause. A retry will therefore see `already_gone: True` (idempotent path), masking the underlying upstream failure.

items.name: agent/complete
items.summary: L1 one-shot completion via Anna server's `POST /copilot/app/complete`. The bridge transparently mints a throw-away app session under the `sampling_token` (ttl 120s), issues the request, then deletes the session in a `finally` block — plugins never see the underlying token. **Not** sugar over `sampling/createMessage` (that path runs through the host's own model); this hits the user's Anna server. **Note:** the backing session is minted with `kind='agent'` (not `kind='complete'`) and used purely as transport — Anna server's `/copilot/app/complete` endpoint accepts any agent-kind app-session token, and the same MCP completion shape is returned. Behaviour matches the `anna-app` SDK's `llm.complete`; callers wanting a strict `kind='complete'` session row must issue `session.create({kind: 'complete'})` + the HTTP `/copilot/app/complete` path manually. Use this when you only need a single model reply with no tools and no multi-turn history; for stateful tool-using runs use `session.create` + `session.run`.
items.signature: complete(*, messages: list[dict], maxTokens: int | None = None, modelPreferences: dict | None = None, systemPrompt: str | None = None, temperature: float | None = None, stopSequences: list[str] | None = None, metadata: dict | None = None) -> dict

params.name: messages
params.summary: Non-empty array of MCP-shaped messages (`{role, content}`).
notes: Validated bridge-side: must be a list with at least one entry.
Anna server applies the same schema constraints as the `anna-app` SDK; multimodal content blocks are accepted verbatim.

params.name: maxTokens
params.summary: Hard cap on response tokens; must be `> 0` when supplied.

params.name: modelPreferences
params.summary: MCP-style model hint, e.g. `{"hints": [{"name": "gpt-4o"}], "costPriority": 0.2}`.
notes: Camel-case to match the MCP wire spec and Anna server's `_CompleteBody.modelPreferences` field.
Anna server may ignore hints that fall outside the user's enabled model set.

params.name: systemPrompt
params.summary: System prompt prepended on Anna server for this single call.

params.name: temperature
params.summary: Sampling temperature; passes through unchanged.

params.name: stopSequences
params.summary: Stop strings forwarded to the upstream model.

params.name: metadata
params.summary: Opaque metadata echoed in audit logs; not interpreted by the model.

returns.desc:
MCP-style completion: `{content, model, usage}`.

- **`content`** — list of content blocks (typically `[{type: 'text', text: ...}]`); matches `sampling/createMessage` output shape.
- **`model`** — the model id actually used by Anna server (may differ from a `modelPreferences` hint).
- **`usage`** — token accounting `{input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens}` when the provider reports it.

Returned verbatim from `/copilot/app/complete`; the bridge does not reshape or filter the response.

errors.name: AGENT_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: `sampling_token` missing from handler `ctx`. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_NOT_GRANTED`.

errors.name: INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: `_validate_complete` rejected the body (e.g. empty `messages`, non-positive `maxTokens`). SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`.

errors.name: QUOTA_EXCEEDED
errors.desc: User plan-level LLM quota exhausted (either at mint time or at complete time). Propagated verbatim from upstream. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`.

errors.name: PROVIDER_ERROR
errors.desc: Catch-all: backing-session mint failed, `/copilot/app/complete` raised 5xx, or response was malformed. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR`. The throw-away session is always torn down in `finally` — a `PROVIDER_ERROR` here does **not** leak quota.

errors.name: RATE_LIMITED
errors.desc: Provider rate-limited the completion. Propagated verbatim from upstream. SDK constant: `AGENT_ERR_RATE_LIMITED`.

limitations: ⚠ **Wire `error_name` ≠ SDK constant** — see `session.create` Known limitations.

⚠ **Backing session is `kind='agent'`, not `kind='complete'`.** Per `agent.py:_complete` NOTE, Nexus mint always derives `kind='agent'` from this body shape; the L1 path uses an L2 agent session as transport. Same backing thread, but a strict `kind='complete'` session row requires the explicit `session.create({kind: 'complete'})` path. Behaviour-wise indistinguishable for the caller (same MCP completion shape returned), but the audit log will show an agent-kind app_session.
**No `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` possible** — the bridge manages the uuid internally and tears it down before returning. Plugins never see the backing `app_session_uuid`.

**Post-complete delete is best-effort.** If the teardown call in `finally` fails (e.g. network blip), it is logged at DEBUG and silently swallowed; the throw-away session may linger until Anna server's own TTL (120s) expires. The plugin still gets a successful completion response.
